figures.label: S2
figures.caption: Figure S2: Voltage profiles of operando cells during lithiation of the a) bismuth, b) indium c) silver d) magnesium interlayers. Atomic percentages of the average composition of the inter- layer based on amount of plated lithium are shown on the top x-axis. Due to kinetic effects the lithiation behavior shown by the voltage profile deviates from the phase diagram. The voltage observed at any point reflects the primary electrochemical reaction, essentially, the phase with the lowest potential. Heterogeneous lithiation of the interlayer leads to these phases forming earlier due to local lithium concentrations being higher than the average composition. As seen from the operando images the relatively fast diffusivity phases are preferentially lithiated, driving this heterogeneity, nucleating the successive phases, the potentials of which are observed in the voltage profile. figures.label: S8
figures.caption: Figure S8: Overpotential at lithium metal nucleation on the working electrode with and without sputtered interlayers. Measured in 3 electrode cells, Fig. S7. Data points are taken from the lowest point at which the nucleation overpotential spike reaches. Mg shows only a gradual decrease with no nucleation overpotential. The indium, silver and magnesium interlayers do not show a nucleation overpotential spike typically seen in anodeless cells when nucleating metallic lithium at the SE interface (Fig. S8). Bismuth has a nucleation overpotential of 10 mV, likely due to contact loss with the solid electrolyte upon fracturing. Alloying interlayers reduce the surface energy for metallic lithium to nucleate, thus leading to a lower overpotential. figures.label: S12
figures.caption: Figure S12: XPS spectra taken insitu during magnesium interlayer sputtering and electrochemi- cal lithiation. Dashed lines show the difference in peak shifts between the S-metal peak and the pristine Li-S peak. No peak shift back to the Li2S species is seen immediately after lithiation. Mg also forms more phosphide compounds compared with the other interlayers, seen by higher intensity peaks in the P 2p spectra.
